issue.body:
This is in the very early stages.  There are still a *lot* of tests that fail, but on the other hand, there also are a lot that pass, so that's something!

As much as possible, I'm trying to replace calls to functions that have been eliminated with their modern equivalents.  Only when I can't find any modern equivalent, I fall back on the `tf.compat.v1` packages.

I found a couple of places where we were still using `tf.contrib` features.  One was a function that has moved to the tensorflow-probability package, so I added that as a dependency.  The other was the PowerSign optimizer which has been completely eliminated, so I removed support for it.

In TensorFlow 2, Tensor objects are no longer hashable, which means they can't be used as keys in dicts anymore.  As a workaround for that, they allow you to get a hashable reference to a Tensor by calling the `experimental_ref()` method.  As the name suggests, that feature is still experimental and may change in the future.  I'm using it anyway because I don't see any other clean way of handling this.  We'll need to keep an eye on what happens with it in future versions.

I'm not making any effort to convert TensorGraph.  The plan is to remove it in the next release.  That means we need to decide what to do about the remaining models that are based on it, as dicussed in #1732.
